title: Natalia Ginzburg's birth chart
metaDescription: Natalia Ginzburg's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 21.6° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Five of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Cancer — the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Saturn and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 21.6° Cancer — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by Jupiter. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Cancer and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Mercury holds 6.3° Cancer, Venus holds 5.6° Cancer, Mars holds 24.8° Virgo — in the old shorthand, a mind that absorbs before it argues; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Jupiter and Pluto — a sextile holding at 0.6°. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift. Behind it, Jupiter square Neptune at 0.7°, and Mercury conjunction Venus at 0.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Moon in Capricorn at 10.5° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Cancer at 20.3° is in detriment. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives water 5, earth 3, air 1, fire 1, and cardinal 6, fixed 3, mutable 1 across the modes. A water emphasis keeps long books: little is forgotten, and nothing is felt only once. Venus and Uranus were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Capricorn for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 15.2° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 10.5°.
